descriptionHtml:
Approach · EFS Empty & Failure States · S24 Screenshot pack: one screenshot of each of the 10 states, attached to the UAT

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T3 A screenshot of each of the 10 states, as built, is attached to the UAT so testers know what 'correct' looks like. (TFA-94745 AC 8; UAT EFS intro)
  • U11 Every state shows a clear, plain-language message in the app's existing style that tells the physician what to do next (retry, enable permission, sign in, check connection). (UAT EFS Expected Result; TFA-94745 AC 1; TFA-94745 AC 5)
  • U14 Every state works in both Hospital and Nursing Home, on web, iOS and Android. (UAT EFS Expected Result; UAT 3.3; TFA-94745 AC 6)

Test design technique: Happy path (happy-path) — Walk the normal flow exactly as the UAT / ticket words it; everything it names has to show up.

Given The screenshots saved by S01, S02, S06 to S11, S14, S16, S17 and S27 (web, both contexts) and S18 (iOS, Android)

When Pick one per state, label each with the state number, attach them under the EFS table in the UAT doc; add per-context and per-platform shots where they exist

Then All 10 states have a screenshot; Daniela confirms they show what 'correct' looks like

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Document check against TFA-94745 AC 8: a missing state is a Fail. Per-context and per-platform shots are a note, not a Fail, until Q3 says they are required. The attach step is done by Quinn or Daniela, never by the agent; it also settles the 'existing style' reference (Q3)

Where it ran: local code-review (judged by reading the code); test method DOC · Document check; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S24 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/EFS.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane code-review.

Test method: DOC · Document check; secondary: VISUAL · Visual (screenshots for a person) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: code-review.
